This is consistent with a policy that must choose among up/down/left/right/no-op on a 10×10 grid. The input specification itself is the strongest clue: 5 binary channels exactly matching agent, moving objects, reward targets, obstacles, and previous frame, with a wall border around an 8×8 playable area and a 5-action space including no-op.

Reasoning: The combination of 5 channels, 5 actions (`no-op, up, down, left, right`), a 10×10 grid with a wall border, and a previous-frame channel is the signature of the MinAtar game **Asterix**. Breakout/Pong/Freeway are ruled out by their action spaces (left/right or up/down only) and lack of reward targets. Snake and Sokoban do not naturally have this exact 5-channel/5-action setup with a previous-frame channel. Asterix has exactly these channels: player, enemies, treasure, walls, and previous frame, and the agent moves in four directions while collecting treasure and avoiding enemies.

Description: The agent controls Asterix on a 10×10 grid, moving up/down/left/right to collect treasure (reward targets) while avoiding enemies (moving objects). Collecting treasure gives reward; touching an enemy ends the episode or gives negative reward.
